story_review.one_viewing_summary: Intended chain from code, at counter level. A door shuts on an empty stand where an apron hangs, and the phone rings while two tables wait. Then comes the same stand in the closed room, with chairs up and the door shut. A dark panel on the stand lights, writes Haniya and AI host beside the apron, and silences the ringing phone, its lamp steady under voice rings, as the lights go out. A guest's phone beside the code opens a menu, a dish is tapped and Pay turns to Paid. The mark reaches the printer, a ticket prints and the cook starts the wok. The owner's $9,650 is stamped as his own count. Coins fill a jar under a FOX 26 tag. The rule card and the blank folder box follow. The same guest's phone times out beside a quote, and the panel takes an order while the jar takes its two tags.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The new s2 answers the opening question on the same stand without any performer. The panel takes the station and the call, which is literal to the pivoted line 2 (c1, c2, c5). The close answers within source limits. A's remaining failures are in how the hook, s3 and s9 are pictured, not in the story order.
story_review.weakest_transition: s8 to s9 at 49.4 s. Cutting from the blank folder box to the s3 guest's own hand and phone invites the false inference that the same guest failed to scan.

strongest_frame: s2 host-panel:a close, 10.89 to 13.23 s. At stand scale 1.9 the phone that has rattled since s1 goes quiet (10.89 to 11.29 s), its line lamp holds steady and voice rings travel to it from the lit Haniya panel. That gives the hook's unanswered phone its answer on the same object. This is code only.
weakest_frame: s9 quote-card:a medium, 51.21 to 53.81 s. The s3 guest's phone lies flattened on the table and its screen times out beside the quote card, so the customer's limit is carried by text.
